label: Flood response and floodplain management
description: The organizations whose job is flood response: a county flood program (emergency management with floodplain administration and public works), a levee or drainage district, or a regional flood warning program. Plans and products: the county emergency operations plan and flood annex, the National Weather Service river forecast and Ready, Set, Go water resources products (NWS Instruction 10-922), flood categories per forecast point (NWS Manual 10-950), the levee district's flood fight plan, and the community's National Flood Insurance Program floodplain ordinance. Variants: a county flood program (emergency manager, floodplain administrator, public works), a levee or drainage district (operator, patrols, pumps) and a regional flood warning program (gauge network, warning dissemination).

vocabulary.facility: the river reach, the levee system and the county's roads, crossings, pump stations and critical facilities
vocabulary.public: residents and businesses in the floodplain, motorists, campers and farm families
vocabulary.frontline: road crews, levee patrol staff, pump operators, 911 dispatchers, deputies, volunteer fire and rescue

it: EOC software and the incident log
county GIS with parcels, critical facilities and floodplain layers
mass notification system and Wireless Emergency Alert access
road closure status board and 511 feed
National Water Prediction Service gauge pages and USGS gauge data
ot: gauge telemetry (radio, cellular, satellite) and local rain gauges
variable message signs and road closure signs
NOAA Weather Radio and radio systems
backup generators at pump stations and shelters

roles.name: County Emergency Manager (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns activation, evacuation orders, shelters, requests to the state and the public warning.

roles.name: Floodplain Administrator
roles.description: Owns the flood maps, permits, community flood program and the substantial-damage estimates after the event.

roles.name: Public Works Director / Road Superintendent
roles.description: Owns road and bridge closures, barricades, pumps, debris removal and pump stations.

roles.name: Levee or Drainage District Operator
roles.description: Owns the flood fight: patrols, sandbagging, boils and seepage, closure structures and pumps.

roles.name: Flood Warning Program Coordinator (Gauge Network)
roles.description: Owns the local gauge network, the readings the EOC sees and the dissemination of warnings.

roles.name: Logistics Section Chief
roles.description: Owns sandbag and pump requests, deliveries, shelters supplies and mutual aid.

roles.name: Fire and Rescue Chief (Swift Water)
roles.description: Owns swift water rescue teams, boats and the rescue priorities.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns messages that match the forecast category and the actions asked of residents.

outsideParties: the National Weather Service forecast office
state emergency management and the National Guard
the US Army Corps of Engineers district
volunteer organizations for muck-out and boats
mediaChannels: residents' photos of water over a road on Facebook and Nextdoor
a storm chaser's post on X/Twitter
the regional TV station's river-level graphic
the county emergency management Facebook page
a farm and ranch group chat
a camp or school parent text thread

sceneAnchors.public: on a county road at a low-water crossing: brown water rising over the pavement, a road-closed barricade, wet grass, gray sky, daylight
sceneAnchors.control: inside a county emergency operations center: a wall map of the river with colored zones, laptops, a whiteboard of road closures, staff with radios and coffee, fluorescent light
sceneAnchors.exterior: on a river levee crest at dusk: a gravel patrol road, stacked sandbags, a pump with a discharge hose, a swollen river beside farm fields

addedThreatFamilies.label: River flood
addedThreatFamilies.description: A river rises over days toward a forecast crest that changes with each forecast; closures, sandbagging, a levee fight and evacuations follow the stage.

phaseArc.title: Outlook and watch (Ready, Set)
phaseArc.goal: Players see a hydrologic outlook and a flood watch and decide what to prepare before the river is high.
beats: A hydrologic outlook names the river and the expected rain
The river is rising but still below action stage
A flood watch is issued for the reach

phaseArc.title: Action and flood stage
phaseArc.goal: The river passes action stage and then flood stage; the first closures and the first sandbag requests test the stage-driven plan.
beats: The gauge passes action stage and the first crossing goes under
A flood warning is issued with a forecast crest
Sandbag and pump requests arrive from the district and farms

phaseArc.title: Forecast changes category
phaseArc.goal: A revised forecast raises the crest into a higher category and forces evacuation and flood fight decisions on the latest forecast, not the stale one.
beats: The forecast crest is revised up one category
The levee patrol reports seepage
An evacuation order for a reach is weighed against clearance time and shelter space

phaseArc.title: Crest, recession and re-entry
phaseArc.goal: The river crests and falls slowly; re-entry, damage assessment and recovery decisions begin.
beats: The crest passes and the stage begins to fall
Residents ask when they can return
Substantial-damage estimates and muck-out requests begin

decisionPointExamples: order the evacuation of the east reach now on the revised crest, or wait for the next forecast and risk the clearance time
close the Mill Road crossing at action stage or keep it open for the hospital shift change
commit the last sandbag crews to the levee reach with seepage or to the water plant
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a gauge reading ahead of the forecast, a revised forecast issuance time, a seepage or boil report from a levee patrol, an upstream gauge already above flood stage
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a road under water that cuts the sandbag supply route, a gauge that stops reporting at the worst time, a pump with no fuel, a shelter that fills early
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the NWS forecast office and River Forecast Center, and the levee or drainage district
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Use the point's own flood category stages; flood stage is not bankfull, and minor, moderate and major categories may not all exist at a point. Show the forecast crest changing with an issuance time. Stage is in feet with the gauge's datum, flow in cfs, times in local time with the gauge's time zone. Closures and evacuations should be tied to a stage, not to the clock alone.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Flash flood
addedThreatFamilies.description: Heavy rain over a small basin; water rises in minutes to hours at crossings, creeks, campgrounds and underpasses, often at night, and warnings carry damage threat tags.

phaseArc.title: Rain over the basin
phaseArc.goal: Heavy rain is reported and a flood watch is in effect; players decide whether to pre-position.
beats: A flood watch for excessive rainfall covers the county
Rain gauges report inches per hour
A school or camp asks whether to shelter in place or move

phaseArc.title: Warning and rapid rise
phaseArc.goal: A flash flood warning is issued, possibly tagged; the warning must reach people who are asleep or off the grid.
beats: A flash flood warning is issued with a damage threat tag
A creek rises several feet in an hour
911 receives calls from a low-water crossing

phaseArc.title: Rescues and flash flood emergency
phaseArc.goal: Multiple swift water rescues stretch resources; a flash flood emergency raises the threat.
beats: Swift water teams are committed at two sites
A flash flood emergency is declared for a downstream area
Cell service fails at the camp

phaseArc.title: Recession, search and reunification
phaseArc.goal: Water falls; search, accountability and family reunification dominate.
beats: The creek recedes and roads stay closed
A head count at the camp does not match the roster
A reunification point is opened

decisionPointExamples: evacuate the low camp to higher ground in the dark now, or hold until the creek is seen to rise
send the only boat team to the crossing or hold it for the downstream camp
send a Wireless Emergency Alert for the whole county or only the warned polygon
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a rain gauge total, a 911 call about water over a road, a gauge on a small creek jumping, the warning polygon and its tag
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: no sirens in the county, no cell coverage, a bridge washed out, rescue teams already committed
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the NWS forecast office and 911 dispatch
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Flash flood warning tags are base, CONSIDERABLE and CATASTROPHIC; Wireless Emergency Alerts go out only for CONSIDERABLE and CATASTROPHIC, and CATASTROPHIC is used only with flash flood emergency language. Time between rain and rising water is minutes to hours. A night case must show how the warning reaches sleeping people.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Levee or dam breach
addedThreatFamilies.description: A levee overtops or fails, or high pool and a dam problem force releases and downstream warning; the flood side is warning, evacuation and inundation timing.

phaseArc.title: High water against the levee
phaseArc.goal: Patrols watch a levee under sustained high water.
beats: Patrols report seepage
A sand boil appears behind a reach
The forecast stage nears the levee crest

phaseArc.title: Flood fight
phaseArc.goal: Sandbag rings and ring levees compete for crews and material.
beats: A boil is ringed with sandbags
A second boil appears
Material runs short

phaseArc.title: Breach or overtopping
phaseArc.goal: Water breaches or overtops; warning and evacuation of the protected area must beat the water.
beats: A breach is reported at a reach
The area behind the levee begins to flood
Evacuation routes flood in sequence

phaseArc.title: Rescue and recovery
phaseArc.goal: Rescue, shelter and damage assessment follow; the breach is sealed or the pool is lowered.
beats: Boats work the flooded neighborhood
The district starts closing the gap
Substantial-damage assessment begins

decisionPointExamples: evacuate the whole protected area on a seepage report now, or hold crews at the boil and risk a breach without warning
deliberately cut a lesser levee to relieve pressure and flood farmland, or hold and risk the town
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a patrol report of seepage or a boil, a piezometer reading, a gauge near the levee crest, a call from a dam operator about releases
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a haul road under water, no sand on hand, crews at the limit of shifts
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the levee or drainage district and the US Army Corps of Engineers district
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: A dam owner's emergency action plan stays with the dam; the flood response side is downstream warning, evacuation and inundation timing. Leveed points may show impacts only at moderate or major categories.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Urban and stormwater flooding
addedThreatFamilies.description: Intense rain overwhelms drains: flooded underpasses, transit, basements, combined sewer overflow and pump station failure.

phaseArc.title: Heavy rain
phaseArc.goal: Rain exceeds drain capacity.
beats: Streets pond
An underpass is reported flooding
A transit line reports delays

phaseArc.title: Closures and rescues
phaseArc.goal: Vehicles are trapped and closures cascade.
beats: A vehicle is stuck in an underpass
A pump station loses power
A hospital access road closes

phaseArc.title: Overflow and service loss
phaseArc.goal: Sewer overflow, power and transit losses affect the public.
beats: A combined sewer overflow starts
A substation is threatened
A boil or contact notice is considered

phaseArc.title: Pump-out and recovery
phaseArc.goal: Pumping, cleanup and damage reports.
beats: Pumps are brought in
Underpasses reopen in sequence
Residents report basement damage

decisionPointExamples: close the underpass and reroute the buses now, or keep service running through the peak
divert the overflow to the river and accept a discharge violation, or let streets flood
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a camera on an underpass, a rain gauge total, a pump station alarm, a 311 surge
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a pump station without power, a barricade shortage, traffic that blocks pump trucks
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: public works and the transit agency

addedThreatFamilies.label: Ice jam flooding
addedThreatFamilies.description: Ice jams back water up a river in winter or at breakup; the stage rises quickly and can fall as quickly when the jam releases.

phaseArc.title: Breakup begins
phaseArc.goal: Ice begins to move.
beats: Warm rain on snow
Ice moves at a bend
The gauge rises abruptly

phaseArc.title: Jam and backwater
phaseArc.goal: A jam forms and water rises upstream of it.
beats: Water backs up into a neighborhood
A road floods with ice blocks
A warning is issued

phaseArc.title: Release
phaseArc.goal: The jam releases and a surge moves downstream.
beats: The jam fails
A downstream gauge jumps
Residents downstream have minutes

phaseArc.title: Aftermath
phaseArc.goal: Ice and debris damage and cleanup.
beats: Ice debris on roads
A bridge is inspected
Cleanup requests begin

decisionPointExamples: evacuate the backwater neighborhood now, or wait for the jam to release and risk a surge downstream
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a gauge that rises without rain, a ranger report of an ice dam, a river camera
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a gauge frozen or iced, roads with ice debris, cold-weather shelter needs
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the NWS forecast office and the downstream community
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Stage at an ice-affected gauge can be unreliable; the exercise should say when a reading is estimated.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Flood after wildfire
addedThreatFamilies.description: Rain on a recent burn scar sends flash floods and debris flows down slopes with little warning.

phaseArc.title: Burn scar and forecast rain
phaseArc.goal: A burn scar sits upstream of a community and rain is forecast.
beats: A burn scar assessment names a risk
A flash flood watch with a burn scar tag
Pre-positioning is debated

phaseArc.title: Short-fuse warning
phaseArc.goal: A warning and evacuation order are issued in minutes.
beats: A flash flood warning with an expected rainfall rate on a burn scar
A debris flow blocks a road
A bridge is threatened

phaseArc.title: Debris flow and rescues
phaseArc.goal: Debris flows damage homes; rescues are slow.
beats: A debris flow reaches homes
A road is cut by debris
A shelter opens

phaseArc.title: Recovery and next storm
phaseArc.goal: Cleanup while another storm is forecast.
beats: Another storm is forecast
Debris basins are full
Re-entry rules are debated

decisionPointExamples: order evacuation of the canyon community ahead of a forecast storm, with the costs of repeated evacuations, or wait for rainfall rates to confirm
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a rain gauge rate above the burn scar threshold, a debris basin level, a ranger report
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a road blocked by debris, an evacuation route through the burn scar
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the NWS forecast office and the land management agency that holds the burned area
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: The earth sciences toolkit holds the debris flow hazard material; this family covers the flood response and warning side.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Flood warning service degradation
addedThreatFamilies.description: The tools that warn about floods fail during a flood: a gauge or telemetry is lost, a forecast or dissemination system is out, a pump station loses power, or a warning is missing or wrong.

phaseArc.title: Normal watch
phaseArc.goal: A normal river watch begins.
beats: The gauge reports normally
Rain is forecast
A routine call with the forecast office

phaseArc.title: Loss of data
phaseArc.goal: A key gauge stops reporting while the river rises.
beats: The gauge stops reporting
Another gauge shows a rise
Staff debate what the missing reading means

phaseArc.title: Decide without the number
phaseArc.goal: Players decide closures and evacuation without the gauge, using upstream gauges, cameras and patrols.
beats: A patrol reports water on a road
The forecast office issues a statement that its forecast for the point is suspended
A false social media post gives a stage

phaseArc.title: Restore and review
phaseArc.goal: The gauge is restored and the team compares decisions with the record.
beats: Telemetry returns with a gap in the record
The crest is higher than the team believed
A review of the warning chain begins

decisionPointExamples: close the crossings on an upstream gauge and a patrol report, or wait for a verified reading
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a flat-lined gauge, a mismatch between two gauges, a camera image, a patrol report
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: no sirens, radio coverage gaps, a stale forecast still on a public display
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the NWS forecast office and the USGS Water Science Center
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Missing data is not zero. The exercise should show how players tell a failed gauge from a falling river.

noiseExamples: a dispatcher's question about a routine parking complaint
a request for a permit inspection that day
a call about a mosquito spraying schedule
a vendor asking about pump parts pricing
pressureExamples: a resident posting a photo of water over a road with a wrong stage
a county commissioner asking whether to evacuate before the next forecast
a local TV station showing a different crest than the forecast
a farm owner demanding the levee district save his fields first
a nursing home asking for transport before a closure
a camp director calling about a creek at night
